requirements.requirement: Add at least 512 MB of disk-backed swap on node1 that is active and preferred over any existing swap.
requirements.summary: A 536,870,912-byte regular swap file is active with 524,284 KiB usable capacity and priority 100. Baseline evidence directly showed no existing active swap, so there was no competing swap with a higher priority.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the added swap activates automatically at boot.
requirements.summary: The fstab entry specifies priority 100. A bounded reboot was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, and the recovered system directly showed swapfile.swap active, the swap present in /proc/swaps, and a successful current-boot activation journal entry.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the existing platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after execution, node1 remained on CentOS Stream 10 with kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64. The implementation used the platform's installed util-linux and systemd facilities, and post-execution package health remained clean.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Node1 has a secure 512 MiB disk-backed swap file at priority 100, and a directly observed reboot demonstrated automatic recovery. The mandatory restart evidence is coherent: it includes pre-restart identity and healthy swap state, restart acknowledgement and disconnection, a different post-restart identity, and recovered system, swap, configuration, and file state. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart, while the OS release and kernel remained unchanged.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating, securing, labeling, initializing, persisting, and activating /swapfile directly served the swap outcomes; the scheduled reboot directly tested boot persistence and the mandatory restart protocol. No executor-caused failed services, unsafe socket exposure, package damage, or abandoned temporary files were observed after recovery.
